digest.component_or_area: plan review criterion gating / LLM router pre-filter
propositions: Four criteria (T13, T14, removal-rationale, asserted-capability) produced zero findings across ~7,900 agentic runs due to over-broad or missing trigger vocabulary, necessitating deterministic pre-filters to skip LLM routing when criterion subject vocabulary is entirely absent.

Deterministic gate rules are implemented as frozen dataclasses with text_all (regex conjunction), file_impact_globs (fnmatch patterns), and file_impact_reason_re fields, firing when ANY arm matches, and skip records are surfaced in coverage.routing.det_gated keyed by criterion id.

Overlay criteria (T13, T14) extend _DET_OVERLAY_RULES in registry.py; leaf-routed criteria (removal-rationale, asserted-capability) use a parallel _DET_LEAF_GATE_RULES table with a new gate block in orchestrator.route_criteria, avoiding duplication by recording skips only at the assemble step.

asserted-capability gates on conjunction of two text_all legs (module-ref and capability-verb), firing only when both match, and all migrated T5a/T5d/T7/T12 rules preserve existing fire/no-fire behavior as one-element text_all tuples without file_impact arms.

Audit-validated trigger regexes for T13 (enforcement-vocabulary), T14 (scheduler/release/workflow-vocabulary plus .github/* glob), removal-rationale (removal-vocabulary plus file_impact reason regex), and asserted-capability (capability-verb conjunction) achieve 84–96.5% fire rates over 743 reviewed non-bug tickets.

The pre-filter is conservative and does not reinstate lexical applicability judgment; fired plans route through the unchanged LLM router exactly as before, and the contract and zero-findings evidence are recorded in an ADR 0034 amendment note.
